title: PhD scholarship in Development of High Temperature Heat Pumps with Thermal Energy Storage - DTU Construct
description:
Do you want to start your research career by making industrial heat clean, flexible and affordable? At DTU Construct you will work at the forefront of technologies key to decarbonizing industries: high-temperature heat pumps and high-temperature thermal energy storage.We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps and thermal energy storage. Your project will develop new Carnot Battery technologies: systems that combine heat pumps based on high temperature thermodynamic cycles together with high-temperature thermal energy storage, such as molten salts and dual-media packed beds. These systems will deliver clean process heat while also giving industry flexibility on the electricity market.Supervision: Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson with industrial secondments. Responsibilities and qualificationsYour overall goal will be to find out how industrial high temperature heat pumps can benefit from integrated thermal energy storage by developing new cost-effective, high-performance hybrid configurations. You will work with fellow doctoral candidates across the network and with industrial partners in Denmark and abroad.Your main tasks will be:
  • Develop and Design new architectures comprising cycles using natural working fluids and thermal energy storage, optimised for efficiency, cost, and fast response to electricity price signals
  • Carry out multi-objective optimisation and dynamic system analysis of alternative layouts
  • Validate results by carrying out experiments and data comparison during industrial secondments, turning the results into innovations with real-world impact (e.g. patents, future commercial solutions)
  • Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
You have:
  • A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems
  • Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects
  • Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar
  • Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. We offerDTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.Salary and appointment termsThe appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027, or according to mutual agreement. You can read more about career paths at DTU here.Further informationFurther information may be obtained from Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli, adrsc@dtu.dk and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson, acerl@dtu.dk. You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:
  • A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
  • A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
  • A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on high-temperature heat pumps combined with thermal energy storage (e.g. Carnot Batteries): select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making.
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

title: MHPSS Advisor
description:
Are you an experienced Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) professional with a passion for advancing evidence-based MHPSS practice in humanitarian settings? Danish Red Cross (DRC) is looking for a MHPSS Advisor to provide technical expertise, capacity development, and quality assurance to the Red Cross Red Crescent National Societies (RCRC) National Societies delivering community-based MHPSS interventions in humanitarian settings.

About the position and the assignments  

You will be based at the Danish Red Cross HQ in Copenhagen and will be part of the Health Team in the Technical Quality and Impact Unit of the International Department. The Health Team comprises technical advisors within health and mental health and psychosocial support. It ensures the availability of the necessary technical capacities to provide timely and relevant assistance and advice to DRC-supported operations, with a primary focus on the Africa, while also supporting MHPSS interventions in MENA, Europe and Asia regions as needed.

As a member of the Health Team, you will be working under the line management of the Health Team Lead and will also work closely with other colleagues at the DRC HQ and Regional and Country Offices (COs), as well as with NSs staff and volunteers. You will also collaborate with the colleagues from the International Federation of the Red Cross Red Crescent (IFRC) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The position does not have programme management responsibilities but supports programmes through technical accompaniment, mentoring, and quality assurance.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

  • Strategic planning and direction: Contribute to defining and rollout of DRC’s strategic directions within MHPSS in humanitarian settings. Support development and rollout of strategies, policies, and technical frameworks for MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
  • Technical support and guidance: Provide evidence-based guidance and advice to DRC COs and National Societies on MHPSS priorities, approaches and activities, remotely or through country visits and missions to ensure that MHPSS interventions follow industry standards and good practice. Support development or adaptation and rollout of relevant technical tools and guidelines to meet operational needs.
  • Strengthening of capacities: Support National Societies in assessing technical capacity needs, and in designing and implementing capacity-strengthening plans, including trainings, coaching, mentoring, and technical supervision. 
  • Program monitoring and evaluation:  Support planning and undertaking of assessments, baselines, endlines, reviews and evaluations, and monitoring of MHPSS interventions.
  • Advocacy: In close collaboration with relevant humanitarian diplomacy (HD) colleagues, contribute to DRC’s policy influencing, advocacy and HD efforts on MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
  • Resource mobilisation: Support proposal development by contributing to the design and quality assurance of MHPSS components in the project proposals that align with donor requirements and organisational goals and priorities.
  • Partnerships and collaboration: Foster thematic partnerships and joint MHPSS initiatives within the RCRC Movement and with external stakeholders. 
  • Surge deployments: Undertake MHPSS surge/deployments in support of DRC bi-lateral operations and wider RCRC Movement responses, including multilateral deployments with the ICRC and the IFRC.  

 

Your profile

We are looking for an experienced MHPSS professional with at least five years of experience working on community-based MNHPSS with humanitarian and development organisations, including at least three years in international postings in Africa and MENA regions. You hold a master's degree, or equivalent experience, in MHPSS, social sciences, or another relevant field. You have sound technical, strategy and advisory skills within community-based MHPSS in humanitarian settings and migration. You have proven experience developing and adapting technical guidance, tools and training materials, as well as designing and facilitating capacity-development initiatives for staff and volunteers of partner organisations. 

You have experience supporting assessments, technical reviews, evaluations, and the development of quality assurance processes for community-based MHPSS interventions. You are an excellent facilitator and communicator with strong interpersonal and cross-cultural skills. You work collaboratively, are well organised, and are able to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines. You are willing and able to undertake field missions, including emergency deployments, with travel of up to four months per year. Professional working proficiency in both English and French is required. Experience of working for the International RCRC Movement is considered an asset. 

We offer

A job with an opportunity to improve the lives of the most vulnerable people around the world. We further offer a unique opportunity to influence the strategic development and mainstreaming of MHPSS in humanitarian settings.

The position is a full-time position - 37 working hours per week. The position is 12 months with possibility for extension.

Salary and employment conditions are in accordance with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargaining agreement with HK and AC, depending on experience and qualifications. The position is based at the Danish Red Cross headquarters in Copenhagen and requires on-site presence. As this is a national position based in Denmark, the salary package does not include relocation assistance to Denmark and housing or family-related allowances.

Your future workplace

The International Red Cross and Red Crescent network is the largest humanitarian network in the world, with a presence and activities in almost every country. All Red Cross and Red Crescent activities have one central purpose: to help those who suffer, without discrimination, whether during conflict, in response to natural or man-made disasters, or due to conditions of chronic poverty. Our work is guided by seven fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality. 

DRC’s international department’s approx. 300 staff supporting RCRC NSs with planning and implementing humanitarian and development interventions in some of the most challenging contexts in 20 countries across Africa, MENA, Asia, and Europe.

We offer a meaningful work at a purpose-driven workplace with truly engaged colleagues. We focus on professional challenges, well-being and a flexible organising of your work life. All of us contribute to a great work environment and colleagueship. 

 

Application and further information

For any specific questions about the position, please contact us at zesd@rodekors.dk subject “MHPSS Advisor 2026”.

Interviews will take place in the second part of November with an expected start date as soon as possible and no later than 01 January 2027. 

We look forward to receiving your application and CV no later than 18 November 2026. Application and CV in English are accepted only through our online recruitment system. Applications made by email will not be reviewed.

title: Gram Equipment Graduate Program
description:
Unleash your potential in the Gram Equipment Graduate talent program - Experience hands-on learning in real business settings, open doors to global career opportunities, and join a community of change-makers!

About Us:

Gram Equipment is a global leader in providing innovative solutions for the ice cream and dairy industry. We are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of technology and driving forward the future of our industry. As part of our commitment to nurturing talent and fostering excellence, we are excited to announce our Graduate Program, designed to provide an immersive experience for aspiring professionals who are passionate about both mechanical engineering and commercial business.

Program Overview:

Our Graduate Program offers a unique opportunity for candidates with diverse backgrounds to gain a well-rounded experience in our organization. The program spans a duration of 24 months, divided into four rotations of six months each. This structure ensures that participants gain a comprehensive understanding of both mechanical engineering and commercial aspects of our business.

Qualifications:

We are seeking candidates who have or will graduate either in 2026 or in 2027, and who meet the following criteria:

  • Mechanical Engineering Background with Commercial Interest:

Candidates with a mechanical engineering background who possess a strong interest in commercial business and project management.

  • Commercial Engineering Background with Mechanical Engineering Interest:

Candidates with a commercial/business-oriented Engineering background who are keen to explore the world of mechanical engineering.

Key Program Highlights:

  • Mentorship: Participants will have the opportunity to work closely with a personal mentor from our global management team, offering valuable insights and guidance throughout the program.
  • Continuous Development: Gram Equipment is committed to fostering the growth and development of its talent. Participants will have access to the Gram Academy, a platform dedicated to ongoing learning and skill development.
  • International Rotation: Possibility for an international 6 month rotation in either our Turkish or US location.
  • Community Building: Join a vibrant and peer -based community of talented individuals within our organization, creating opportunities for networking, knowledge sharing, and collaboration.

How to Apply & Our Recruitment Process:

Our recruitment process is designed to identify and nurture potential talent. We believe in comprehensive evaluation, from video interviews and cognitive assessments to in-depth interviews and real-world business case evaluations during the Assessment Day, ensuring we welcome the best fit for our Graduate Program.

  1. Application and Assessment: Apply before 1st of March 2027, and if shortlisted, you'll complete a video interview and cognitive assessment.
  2. Interview and Evaluation: Promising candidates proceed to a comprehensive evaluation phase, which evaluates their behavioral competencies and business acumen, including a detailed assessment of a business case.
  3. Contract and Start Date: Upon impressing us at every stage, you'll sign a contract and officially begin your journey with the Gram Equipment Graduate Program on 1st of September 2027.

Join Us in Shaping the Future:

At Gram Equipment, we believe that innovation is driven by diverse perspectives and talents. Join our Graduate Program to embark on a journey that will equip you with the skills, knowledge, and experiences needed to excel in both the mechanical engineering and commercial aspects of our dynamic industry.

We look forward to welcoming the next generation of leaders to our team.

“For me, the biggest value being part of the Gram Equipment Graduate Program has been the people I have worked with along the way and the understanding I have gained of how the different parts of the organization come together.”Tommy Bui (ENG Integrated Design - SDU) - Project Manager at Gram Equipment

“The Graduate program gave me a strong network across the entire company and useful insights into many of our internal processes.” / “Contributing to such a significant change as a graduate was both empowering and a clear example of how my work could make a meaningful difference.”Luciana Apachitei (ENG in Global Business Engineering - VIA University College) - Engineering Excellence Project Manager "At Gram Equipment, I have shaped the company's direction and the projects related to it. I have had the chance to choose the projects that interested me. Many of the things I have learned in my studies, I have been able to apply to what I am doing at Gram Equipment, from engineering work to business understanding. I am actively involved in the strategy work, engineering practices and various digitalization tools. I use a lot of theoretical knowledge that I have acquired in my Engineering studies in relation to my daily work. My business background helped me understand how the business is working, and because the company foundation is at the technical aspect, my background has helped me identify its strengths and weaknesses very fast." -Rudy Mandrup Cazelles (ENG Product Development and Innovation - SDU) - Business Developer at Gram Equipment

Gram Equipment is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: kok
description:

Requirements:

title: 1.assistent til SMP - Fyn
description:
Vi søger en erfaren 1.assistent til Fyn

Er du serviceminded og kan lide et job med meget kørsel?

SMP Rengøringsservice er i rivende udvikling og søger derfor en erfaren medarbejder på fuldtid (37t), til vores i forvejen stærke team på Fyn.

Som 1.assistent er dit ansvar at sikre afviklingen af den daglige rengøring i samarbejde med din Serviceinspektør

Andre opgaver kan også forekomme.

Du vil have direkte reference til din Serviceinspektør hos SMP rengøringsservice. Jobbet indebærer b.la. følgende arbejdsområder:

•   Skal stå for rengøring af egne pladser og øvrig bemanding iht. rengøringskalenderen

•   Skabe god relation til kunderne

•   Være behjælpelig med afløsning ved. ferie/sygdom

Det skal forventes, at timer kan ligge både tidlig morgen, eftermiddag og aften.

 

Hvem er du?

 

Vi søger dig, som trives i en omskiftelig hverdag, hvor opgaverne og dagene aldrig er ens.

Det er ikke vigtigt for dig, at du har faste rammer mandag-fredag fra 8-16, men tværtimod trives du med en flydende hverdag, hvor arbejdsugen kan variere med forskellige tidspunkter på dagen.

•   Har erfaring med erhvervsrengøring

•   Står til rådighed for rengøring af egne pladser

•   deler telefonvagt efter forudgående aftale

     står for sidemandsoplæring af rengøringspersonale

•   Kan håndtere og omgås forskellige kulturer

•   Behersker dansk og engelsk i skrift og tale på et rimeligt niveau

•   Har kørekort

•   Kan fremvise straffeattest

Du får stillet en firmabil til rådighed, samt firmatelefon- iPad, og arbejdsbeklædning.

Vi glæder os meget til at lære dig at kende - så hvis du kan se dig selv i denne stilling, bedes du sende din ansøgning til: job@smpservice.dk  - husk at mærke ansøgningen ” 1.assistent Fyn”

 

Samtaler bliver holdt løbende.

 

Har du ikke hørt fra os inden den 04.11.2026, skal du betragte jobbet som besat til anden side.

 

SMP er en velrenommeret virksomhed i rengøringsbranchen, - og det vil vi gerne blive ved med at være

Vi beskæftiger i dag mere end 300 medarbejdere med kunder i en stor del af Danmark. Vi har landsdækkende og lokale aftaler inden for kontor, produktion, skoler, slagterier, bagerier, butikker, supermarkeder mv.

title: Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Switching Leader
description:
Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Electrical Operations / Switching Leader

Location: DenmarkEmployment type: Full-timeEmployer: Global Nordics

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Authorised Person (SAP) / Switching Leader (Koblingsleder) to support electrical operations on a major engineering project in Denmark.

The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating safe switching operations, electrical isolations and safety procedures across high-voltage (HV) and low-voltage (LV) electrical systems.

The position operates within an established electrical safety management structure, under the designated Operation Manager (Driftsansvarlig Person), and in accordance with applicable Danish electrical safety regulations and EN 50110-1.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and oversee HV and LV switching operations.

  • Prepare and review switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

  • Coordinate electrical isolations, earthing and safe access procedures.

  • Prepare, issue and cancel safety documents within the scope of assigned authorisation.

  • Coordinate with Control Engineers and electrical work teams during operational activities.

  • Ensure appropriate safety precautions are implemented before electrical work begins.

  • Supervise and coordinate personnel involved in electrical operational activities.

  • Support commissioning, energisation and electrical system handover.

  • Maintain accurate switching records, operational logs and safety documentation.

  • Participate in safety audits, risk assessments and toolbox talks.

  • Ensure compliance with site-specific electrical safety procedures and applicable Danish regulations.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Relevant qualification in electrical engineering or equivalent professional experience.

  • Extensive experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.

  • Previous experience as a Senior Authorised Person, Switching Leader, Control Engineer or equivalent.

  • Strong understanding of electrical switching, isolation, earthing and safe working procedures.

  • Knowledge of EN 50110-1 and electrical safety management systems.

  • Experience preparing switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate electrical work teams and operational activities.

  • Strong communication, organisational and safety leadership skills.

  • Good command of English.

Electrical Safety Requirements

The successful candidate will undergo a competence assessment and receive the necessary written operational appointment and authorisation under the project's Danish electrical safety management arrangements (KLS-D) before undertaking regulated electrical activities.

The role does not include statutory Operation Manager responsibilities or electrical installation work requiring separate company authorisation.

Application

Please submit your CV, relevant qualifications and details of your professional experience.

title: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
description:
About the positionThe Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.Key responsibilitiesStrategic leadership and governance

  • Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

  • Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

  • Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

  • Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state.

  • Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices.

  • Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.

Operational responsibility

  • Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication.

  • Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.

About youTo succeed in this role, we expect that you:

  • Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage.

  • Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

  • Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions.

  • Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

  • Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.

In addition, you:

  • Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations.

  • Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries.

  • Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.

About the Danish Resilience AgencyThe Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.About the NBCCThe NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.Salary and terms of employmentSalary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. Non-EU/EEA Citizens must hold a valid residence and work permit before you can begin working in Denmark. Citizens of Sweden, Norway, Finland, or Iceland do not require a residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark. For more detailed information regarding the regulations for your specific citizenship, please visit: New to Denmark and/or Info Norden | Nordisk SamarbejdeIf the position is filled by an applicant not currently residing in Denmark, the Danish Resilience Agency is prepared to offer a relocation package of up to 45.000 DKK. Any other costs related to relocation or housing must be covered by the employee.Are you interested?Please submit your application via the “Apply” button on this page. Your application must be received by the recruitment system no later than 15th November 2026 and must include a CV and relevant diplomas of education.For further information about the position, please contact Kia Slæbæk Jensen at +45 2134 1851 or Morten Bro at +45 2178 4257.All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply regardless of personal background.Applications may be shared with participants from the employment committee from all participating countries.

title: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

  1. A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

  2. Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

  3. Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

  4. Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

  5. A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: Automotive Technician
description:
2 positions · Troubleshooting · Test setups · New components · R&D

Do you enjoy figuring out why something does not work? RENTEQ Automotive is looking for two technicians who want to troubleshoot electric vehicles and machines, set up test setups and take part when we develop and test new components. You do not need many years of experience. What matters most is that you are hands on, curious and eager to learn.

About RENTEQ

RENTEQ Automotive is a Danish company at the forefront of electrifying existing diesel machines and vehicles. We develop and produce conversion kits for authorised dealers and end customers, and we work with everything from vans to heavy off highway machines such as dumpers and excavators. We are a growing startup with short decision paths, and our workshop and offices under one roof in Dragør.

The job

You will join our technical team in R&D and work closely with engineers, software developers and mechanics. You will be where things are tested and tried out in practice. One day you are troubleshooting a van, the next you are helping build a test setup for a new component. The work is mainly based in Dragør, but tasks at other locations may occasionally come up.

Your tasks will include:

•       Troubleshoot electrical systems and wiring harnesses on vehicles and machines

•       Set up and maintain test setups, both on the bench and in the vehicles

•       Help test new components and get them installed and integrated

•       Use diagnostic tools and CAN logs to find faults

•       Support engineers and software developers with the hands on work during testing

•       Document faults, solutions and test results so the rest of the team can use them.

Is this you?

You may be newly qualified or have a few years of experience from a workshop or similar. We care more about your troubleshooting skills and willingness to learn than about how long you have been in the trade.

•       Trained as a car mechanic, mechatronics technician, truck mechanic, construction machinery mechanic, electrician or similar

•       Experience with electrical troubleshooting on vehicles or machines

•       Comfortable using a multimeter and diagnostic equipment

•       Hands on, systematic and good at keeping things organised

•       Curious and quick to learn new things

•       Good English skills, Danish is an advantage

It is a plus if you know some of the following, but it is not a requirement:

•       CAN bus and tools such as PCAN, SavvyCAN or similar

•       Electric or hybrid vehicles, or high voltage systems

•       A driving licence for larger vehicles.

What we offer

•       A varied job on many different vehicles and machines

•       The chance to learn a lot about electric vehicles, CAN and high voltage

•       Close collaboration with engineers and software developers, where asking questions and helping each other comes naturally

•       Access to test equipment and modern diagnostic tools

•       An informal team in a growing startup

•       Good facilities, shared lunch and easy access by car or public transport.

Salary

Salary is set individually based on gender neutral criteria: education, work experience and other qualifications. We are happy to share the salary range for your profile before the first interview.

Practical information

•       Number of positions: 2

•       Employment: Permanent, full time

•       Department: R&D

•       Location: Mainly on site in Dragør, with some flexibility by agreement

•       Start date: As soon as possible.

How to apply

Send your CV and a few lines about yourself and your troubleshooting experience to louie@ren-teq.com. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

If you have questions about the position, feel free to contact Louie Lucas Bisgaard Nyeland at louie@ren-teq.com or +45 27812385.

 

RENTEQ Automotive · Dragør, Denmark · www.ren-teq.com

title: Battery Technology Lead
description:
Are you passionate about battery technology? RENTEQ Automotive is looking for someone to lead our testing of battery cells and modules, and to make us ready to switch quickly when new battery technologies reach the market. Many years of experience is not the most important thing. What matters most is that you have a solid background in battery technology, from either work or studies.

About RENTEQ

RENTEQ Automotive is a Danish company at the forefront of electrifying existing diesel machines and vehicles. We develop and produce conversion kits for authorised dealers and end customers, and we work with everything from vans to heavy off highway machines. We are a growing startup with short decision paths and high professional ambitions.

The job

Batteries are at the core of our products, and the technology is moving fast. You will have the main responsibility for our battery testing and for making us ready for new cell types, formats and suppliers. You will also be an important technical voice when we decide how batteries are used in our systems. You will be part of R&D and work closely with our engineers.

Your tasks will include:

•       Plan and carry out tests of battery cells and modules, such as capacity, cycle testing, performance and thermal behaviour

•       Build test setups and processes so we can quickly evaluate and adopt new battery technologies

•       Help select and purchase test equipment and tools

•       Document test results and turn them into clear recommendations

•       Be a technical sparring partner on cell selection and integration into our systems

•       Keep yourself and the team up to date on developments in battery technology

•       Act as the technical link in the design of battery enclosures

•       Communicate with external test facilities when needed.

Is this you?

Your background can come from industry or from your studies. You may be a recent graduate with a strong theoretical foundation, or have hands on experience with battery systems. Both profiles are interesting to us.

•       Background in battery technology, electrochemistry, energy engineering or similar

•       Knowledge of testing battery cells or modules

•       Understanding of safe battery handling

•       Interest in test equipment and test methods

•       Structured and thorough in your documentation

•       Good at explaining technical topics so both engineers and other colleagues understand them

•       Good English skills, Danish is an advantage.

What we offer

•       Main responsibility for an area that is central to our products

•       The opportunity to build our battery testing from the ground up

•       Influence on technology choices and equipment purchases

•       Close collaboration with dedicated engineers in an informal environment

•       Good facilities in Dragør with easy access by car or public transport.

 Salary

Salary is set individually based on gender neutral criteria: education, work experience and other qualifications. We are happy to share the salary range for your profile before the first interview.

title: Automotive Software Engineer
description:
2 positions · Electric vehicles · Broad profile · R&D

Do you want to help create software that runs in real vehicles in your very first week? RENTEQ Automotive is looking for two software people who are curious, learn fast and want to try their hand at a bit of everything. You do not need to be a specialist or have many years of experience. What matters most is that you are adaptable and eager to learn.

About RENTEQ

RENTEQ Automotive is a Danish company at the forefront of electrifying existing diesel machines and vehicles. We convert everything from vans to dumpers and excavators, and all the vehicles run on control software we develop ourselves. We are a growing startup with short decision paths, a small team, and our workshop and offices under one roof in Dragør.

What is it like to work with us?

Our software developers are never far from the product. The workshop is right next door, and the changes you make in the morning can be tested in a vehicle in the afternoon. We are a small team where everyone helps each other, and you will quickly work closely with engineers, mechanics and management.

We do not expect you to know everything from day one. You will get time to learn our system, and support from colleagues working with CAN, embedded software, high voltage and testing. In return, we expect you to be curious, ask questions and be keen to get stuck in.

The job

You will start by getting to know our system: how the vehicles are controlled, how the software is structured, and how it all ties together with CAN and hardware. After that, you will become part of the daily software work and help develop the system further. Our control software is currently built in Simulink, and we are moving parts of it to C/C++, so you will work with both.

Your tasks will include:

•       Get to know our control software and how it works together with the vehicle

•       Flash and test software on the bench and in the vehicles

•       Test new components and help integrate them into the system

•       Debug using CAN logs and measurement data

•       Help develop new features and improve existing ones

•       Document what you learn and build so the rest of the team can use it too.

Is this you?

We are looking for broad profiles rather than specialists. You may be a recent graduate or have a few years of experience. What matters most is that you have a good foundation and a desire to learn.

•       A degree in software, electronics, mechatronics, automation or similar, or equivalent experience

•       Programming experience, for example C, C++, Python or Matlab

•       Curious, adaptable and quick to learn new things

•       You enjoy hands on work and seeing things work in real life

•       Good English skills, Danish is an advantage

It is a plus if you have tried some of the following, but it is not a requirement:

•       Simulink or Stateflow

•       Embedded software or microcontrollers

•       CAN bus and tools such as PCAN or Vector

•       Electric vehicles, batteries or high voltage systems

•       Git.

What we offer

•       A job where you see your software running in real vehicles on the road and on construction sites

•       A fast-paced professional development opportunity with broad insight into software, hardware and electric vehicles

•       A small, informal team where asking questions and helping each other comes naturally

•       Varied tasks on many different vehicles and machines

•       The opportunity to grow with the company and shape how we build our software going forward

•       Workshop and offices in Dragør with easy access by car or public transport.

Salary

Salary is set individually based on gender neutral criteria: education, work experience and other qualifications. We are happy to share the salary range for your profile before the first interview.

Practical information

•       Number of positions: 2

•       Employment: Permanent, full time

•       Department: R&D

•       Location: On site in Dragør

•       Start date: As soon as possible.

How to apply

If you have questions about the position, feel free to contact Louie Lucas Bisgaard Nyeland at louie@ren-teq.com or +45 27812385.

title: A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years.
description:
A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

  • Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

  • Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

  • Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

  • Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

  • Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

  • Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

  • A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

  • First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

  • Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

  • Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

  • A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

  • Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

  • The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

  • Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

  • Experience in psychiatric epidemiology.

  • Experience in the development or validation of prediction models.

  • Practical experience with target trial emulation.

  • Experience in international research collaborations.

  • Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information please contact Professor Trine Munk-Olsen, e-mail: tmun@sdu.dk, phone: +45 24 46 62 97.

Application deadline

November 18, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET).

Interviews

Interviews are expected to take place in early December 2026.

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Postdoc is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed postdoc allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Hospitalsringen 90, 5260 Odense S.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

  • a motivation letter

  • a detailed CV

  • degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma)

  • a complete and numbered list of publications

  • 3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

    • It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

  • a detailed description of research experience

  • an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: Teamlead Reliability Engineers (m/w/d) (Ingenieur/in - Elektrotechnik)
description: Operations and techniciansTeamlead Reliability EngineersImagine a future where you lead an international engineering team that improves the safety, reliability, and performance of our wind farms.Join us in this role where you’ll provide people and technical leadership to the Continental Europe Reliability Engineering team. You’ll set priorities, develop capabilities, and enable consistent, high-quality reliability support across our wind farms. Through data-driven decisions and close collaboration, you’ll help address technical risks, improve asset performance, and strengthen the way we work across sites and turbine platforms. Welcome to Generation CE You’ll be part of WTG Engineering where you, together with your colleagues, will support our operational sites by identifying and addressing technical risks, yield-loss drivers, recurring failures, and improvement opportunities. You’ll connect Reliability Engineers, site teams, CE Engineering, Technical Support, and other specialist functions to coordinate effective corrective and preventive actions. As a team, we share knowledge, support one another, and turn technical insight into practical improvements. We succeed as one by building trust across sites, giving our experts the context and space to make decisions, and keeping safety at the heart of our work. You’ll play an important role in: leading, motivating, and developing an international team of Reliability Engineers through clear objectives, coaching, competence planning, and development conversations translating Generation, CE Engineering, and site priorities into an aligned reliability engineering plan with clear ownership, milestones, and outcomes ensuring structured analysis of reliability performance, yield-loss drivers, recurring failures, technical risks, and emerging trends overseeing root-cause analyses, technical assessments, corrective and preventive actions, and prioritised reliability improvement initiatives strengthening consistent reliability practices, knowledge sharing, and collaboration across operational sites, engineering functions, suppliers, and technical support teams promoting a proactive safety culture and ensuring compliance with asset integrity, HSE, governance, and applicable technical requirements. To succeed in the role, you: have a relevant technical or engineering qualification within mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, reliability, asset management, wind energy, or a comparable field, or equivalent experience bring leadership experience that enables you to develop people, set priorities, allocate resources, and create clarity across an international or multi-site team understand wind turbine operations, reliability engineering, technical support, maintenance engineering, asset integrity, or another high-reliability industry have strong knowledge of reliability and continuous-improvement methods, such as root-cause analysis, trend analysis, failure-mode analysis, reliability-centred maintenance, risk assessment, and corrective-action management can interpret technical and operational performance data and turn your findings into clear priorities, decisions, and measurable improvement actions communicate complex technical matters clearly, build trusted stakeholder relationships, and work professionally in English. Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply. Shape the future with us Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate. As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com (accommodation@orsted.com) . Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position. Position salary range: For this role, the base pay will be determined according to the relevant pay structure for the location where the position is filled. Actual pay will be based on skills, experience, and the expected role fulfilment to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package. Pay details specific to your location will be provided during the interview process.Pre-employment background checks:For certain positions, a background check may be required as part of the hiring process. Because we recruit across multiple countries, the specific checks performed will depend on the role and the legal requirements in the location where the position is filled. If a background check is relevant for the role you are being considered for, you will be informed during the recruitment process. All background checks are carried out by an external provider and always in accordance with applicable local laws and regulations.

title: Vil du være med til at omstille kommunernes økonomi og fremtidssikre velfærden?
description:
Hvordan skaber kommunerne mere handlerum og mest mulig værdi for borgerne? Det kræver nye måder at løse opgaverne på - og du kan være med til at vise vejen. I KL's Omstillings- og Udviklingsenhed kommer du tæt på kommunerne og det politiske maskinrum, hvor rammerne for borgernes hverdag bliver sat. Vil du være med? Vær med til at understøtte kommunernes arbejde med at skabe øget handlerum til borgernær velfærd Som konsulent hos os skal du inspirere kommunerne til at tænke nyt og udvikle deres opgaveløsning, så de får større handlerum til velfærd. Du arbejder på tværs af hele den kommunale forvaltning med de strategiske dagsordener, der præger sektoren. Vi søger dig, der har et stærkt drive og lyst til at omsætte din interesse for kommunernes udvikling til inspiration, der styrker deres muligheder for at levere den bedst mulige velfærd. Omstillings- og Udviklingsenheden leverer inspiration til en bred målgruppe af kommunale politikere, chefer og medarbejdere. Du får derfor berøring med aktuelle dagsordener og forskellige fagområder samt indblik i de tværgående tendenser, udfordringer og muligheder, der kan understøtte et øget økonomisk handlerum i kommunerne. Du kommer desuden til at samarbejde bredt med de forskellige kontorer i KL-huset og får en stor kontaktflade i kommunerne via de mange besøg ud af huset. Enheden er en del af KL's Økonomiske Sekretariat, der bl.a. forhandler den årlige økonomiaftale for kommunerne og er med til at sætte rammerne for den kommunale velfærd. I stillingen vil du dermed få indblik i og bidrage til det politiske maskinrum bag en aftale, der har stor betydning for kommunernes velfærd. Som konsulent i Omstillings- og Udviklingsenheden vil du bl.a. arbejde med at:
  • Kortlægge trends og tendenser på tværs af kommunernes råderumsarbejde
  • Udarbejde understøttende redskaber, fx benchmarking- og selvevalueringsredskaber
  • Identificere og formidle gode eksempler fra kommunerne gennem nyhedsbreve, sociale medier mv.
  • Udvikle og facilitere netværk, temadage, workshops, webinarer, konferencer mv.
  • Afholde inspirationsoplæg og facilitere workshops for byråd og forvaltning i hele landet
  • Udvikle og afprøve nye aktiviteter og redskaber i tæt samarbejde med kommunerne
To konkrete eksempler på opgaver i Omstillings- og Udviklingsenheden fra det seneste år
  • Planlægning og afholdelse af virtuel konference: Hvert år arrangerer enheden den virtuelle konference, Råderumsugen, som giver kommunerne inspiration til, hvordan de kan skabe øget handlerum til borgernær velfærd. Opgaven giver dig mulighed for at gå i dialog med kommunale oplægsholdere, facilitere webinarer som vært i KL's studie og koordinere planlægningen af konferencen, så det opfylder kommunernes ønsker og behov. Siden 2022 har konferencen haft over 1.000 deltagere, og næsten alle kommuner har været repræsenteret. Få indblik i dette års Råderumsuge her. https://tilmeld.kl.dk/raderumsugen-2026/arrangement
  • Facilitering af dialog med kommunalbestyrelser: Enheden har udviklet et koncept, Råderumsspillet, som simulerer en kommunal budgetforhandling og skaber et unikt rum for drøftelser med kommunalbestyrelser om, hvordan kommunen kan omstille og udvikle opgaveløsningen. Som medarbejder i enheden får du mulighed for at facilitere disse sessioner og dermed indgå i en spændende dialog med landets kommunalpolitikere om fremtidens velfærd. Læs mere om konceptet her. https://www.kl.dk/oekonomi-og-administration/oekonomi-og-styring/omstilling-og-udvikling/book-et-oplaeg/raaderumsspillet
Vi søger dig, der med fordel:
  • Har en relevant uddannelsesmæssig baggrund - fx cand.scient.pol., cand.soc., cand.polit. eller cand.scient.adm.
  • Har erfaring fra en kommune, konsulenthus, interesseorganisation eller centraladministrationen
  • Har interesse for at formidle budskaber og viden på en måde, der engagerer kommunerne og kan omsættes til praksis - både skriftligt og mundtligt
  • Har et stærkt drive, kan drive processen for egne opgaver og har et kreativt blik for at udvikle nye aktiviteter
  • Har gode analytiske evner - både kvantitative og kvalitative - og ønsker at udarbejde analyser og viden, der kan anvendes i praksis
  • Har lyst til en omskiftelig hverdag med mange forskelligartede opgaver, opgaver ud af huset og tæt dialog med landets kommuner og andre relevante aktører - fx i forbindelse med kommunebesøg og konferencer
  • Har interesse for de strategiske udfordringer og muligheder, der præger den kommunale sektor - fx arbejdskraftsmangel, det specialiserede socialområde og ny teknologi
Bliv en del af et stærkt fællesskab med en spændende, afvekslende hverdag Som konsulent i KL's Omstillings- og Udviklingsenhed vil du indgå i et team med tre faste medarbejdere. Enheden er en del af et stærkt fagligt og socialt miljø, hvor du bliver kollega med mere end 30 medarbejdere i Økonomisk Sekretariat. Vi vægter socialt samvær og en god stemning højt. Der afholdes løbende sociale aktiviteter i sekretariatet, herunder petanque, fællesspisning og fredagsøl. KL giver desuden mulighed for at deltage i andre aktiviteter efter interesse, bl.a. yoga, fysioterapi, fitness, band, kunstklub, vinsmagning og firmasport. Det praktiske Vi søger en konsulent med tiltrædelse den 1. januar eller hurtigst muligt. Ansøgningsfristen er søndag d. 15. november. Ansættelsesforløbet består af én samtale i uge 47, hvor der indgår en case. Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår følger den gældende overenskomst, og der er mulighed for at forhandle tillæg på baggrund af dine kvalifikationer. Vil du vide mere? Ønsker du yderligere information, er du velkommen til at kontakte specialkonsulent Andreas Hohwy Pallesen på tlf. 3370 3719 eller via e-mail på anhp@kl.dk. KL er interesse- og medlemsorganisation for de 98 kommunalbestyrelser i Danmark. KL bidrager til at udvikle og fastholde et stærkt lokalt demokrati. KL varetager kommunernes fælles interesser og er kommunernes samlede forhandlingsorganisation, videnscenter og forum for fælles initiativer og beslutninger. KL ser forskellighed i medarbejdersammensætningen og i ledelsen som en af vores styrker og opfordrer alle interesserede uanset personlig baggrund til at søge vores ledige stillinger. Kig forbi vores KL Karriereunivers og lær mere om os som arbejdsplads og medarbejdere. https://www.kl.dk/karriereunivers/forside

title: Cafe Flottenheimer is looking for a Floor Manager
description:
Are you passionate about hospitality, quality service, and effective restaurant teamwork? Cafe Flottenheimer is seeking a dedicated and experienced Floor Manager to lead our waiting team and help ensure our guests enjoy an exceptional dining experience every day.

 

About the Role

As Floor Manager at Cafe Flottenheimer, you will coordinate daily front-of-house operations, combining hands-on waiting duties with supervision of the service team. You will work closely with the kitchen to maintain smooth service, a welcoming atmosphere, and consistent standards of guest care.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Welcome guests, take orders, and serve food and beverages

  • Coordinate daily service, allocate sections, and organize waiting staff duties

  • Brief, guide, and train waiting staff to maintain service standards

  • Coordinate orders and service timing with the kitchen team

  • Monitor beverage stocks, arrange replenishment, and minimize waste

  • Handle reservations, guest enquiries, and complaints professionally

  • Oversee payments, opening and closing routines, and dining-area cleanliness

 

Working Conditions

  • Full-time position

  • Work in a guest-facing restaurant environment, outside the kitchen

  • Working hours may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and public holidays

  • Responsibility for maintaining service, hygiene, safety, and operational standards throughout each shift

 

We Expect

  • Solid experience as a Floor Manager, Head Waiter, or in a similar supervisory service role

  • Strong leadership and communication skills, including the ability to coordinate a busy team

  • Knowledge of beverage service, stock control, and payment systems

  • Passion for hospitality and delivering attentive, professional guest service

 

We Offer

  • An exciting and welcoming workplace

  • Salary based on qualifications

  • Opportunity to influence service routines and the development of the waiting team

  • A committed team and professional work environment

 

Sounds interesting? Send your application and CV to info@cafeflottenheimer.dk and become part of Cafe Flottenheimer. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position is available as soon as possible.

The application deadline is 16 November 2026. We look forward to hearing from you.

title: Kok søges til Restaurant Rimini – vi har brug for flere hænder i køkkenet! - Chef Wanted at Restaurant Rimini – Join Our Kitchen Team!
description:

  • Indkøb

  • Nye ideer til menu

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • Arbejder struktureret og har øje for kvalitet og detaljer.

  • Ser dig selv i stillingen som kok.
