title: Investment Analyst / Investment Manager - Green Energy & Infrastructure
employer: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
description:
Are you motivated by making green commercial investments across Africa, Asia, and Latin America?

Impact Fund Denmark is Denmark’s largest impact fund and is internationally recognized as a best-in-class impact investor.  We manage our own private equity funds, debt capital, and concessional capital with a focus on creating sustainable businesses that deliver measurable social, economic and climate impact alongside solid financial returns.

We are strengthening our Green Energy and Infrastructure team and are looking for an Investment Professional to join us in our headquarters in Copenhagen. Depending on your experience, you may join us as Investment Analyst or Investment Manager.

Green Energy and Infrastructure invests in businesses and infrastructure that accelerate the green transition in emerging markets. Our investment focus spans renewable energy, circular economy, electric mobility, and water infrastructure. Through equity and debt investments, active ownership and strategic partnerships, we drive impact and value creation aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. We typically invest between DKK 100-350 million per transaction.

You will be reporting to a Managing Director in Green Energy and Infrastructure and work closely with colleagues in Copenhagen and our regional offices across Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America on investments throughout the investment lifecycle.

 

Investment Analyst

As an Investment Analyst, you will be a key analytical resource in transaction teams, focusing on commercial and financial analysis of investment opportunities.

You will:

  • Screen and analyse new investment proposals using Impact Fund Denmark’s tools and processes.

  • Assist in preparing investment papers, financial analyses and financial modelling.

  • Support due diligence, valuation and deal structuring.

  • Contribute to preparing and presenting investment recommendations and materials for the investment committee and board.

  • Collect and analyse commercial and financial data for deal teams.

  • Help maintain information systems for pipeline tracking and portfolio data.

  • Participate in networking activities to support investment sourcing and promotion.

  • Support project managers in active ownership and portfolio monitoring.

  • Ensure timely and accurate updates of systems with project documents, and financial and sustainability reporting.

  • Assist in assessing exit timing and support execution.

 

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as finance or economics with strong academic results.

  • 1-2 years of relevant experience from impact investing, private equity, M&A, corporate finance or consulting.

  • Solid understanding of financial analysis and valuation.

  • Skilled user of Excel and with an interest in and aptitude for financial modelling.

  • Detail-oriented with a structured working approach.

  • Fluent in English (written and spoken).

  • Curious to broaden your understanding of the world and keen to travel.

 

Investment Manager

As an Investment Manager, you will take the lead on many of the tasks performed by an Investment Analyst. You are thus expected to work independently, drive workstreams, and take ownership of parts of the investment process.

You will:

  • Screen and analyse new investment proposals using Impact Fund Denmark’s tools and processes.

  • Lead preparation of parts of investment papers, financial analyses and financial modelling with guidance from the project manager (Senior Investment Manager or Investment Director).

  • Support and lead due diligence, valuation and deal structuring workstreams.

  • Contribute to preparing and presenting investment recommendations and materials for the investment committee and board.

  • Lead the analysis of commercial and financial data for deal teams.

  • Take part in negotiating terms and drafting legal documentation.

  • Help maintain information systems for pipeline tracking and portfolio data.

  • Participate in networking activities to support investment sourcing and promotion.

  • Support project managers in active ownership and portfolio monitoring.

  • Assist in assessing exit timing and support exit negotiations and execution.

 

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field such as finance or economics with strong academic results.

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience from impact investing, private equity, M&A, corporate finance or consulting.

  • Independent mindset and experienced in owning and managing workstreams.

  • Solid understanding of financial analysis and valuation.

  • Expert user of Excel and with an interest in and aptitude for financial modelling.

  • Detail-oriented with a structured working approach.

  • Fluent in English (written and spoken).

  • Strong interpersonal skills and business judgment.

  • Curious to broaden your understanding of the world and keen to travel.

  • Experience in emerging markets and green energy is an advantage but not a prerequisite.

 

Working at Impact Fund Denmark

Learning is an important element of working in Impact Fund Denmark, and we will support your personal development through training, sparring and by ensuring that you get exciting and challenging tasks and new opportunities for growth. When joining Impact Fund Denmark, you will take part in our extensive onboarding program to get the best possible start in your new role.

We have a diverse and inclusive working environment with more than 170 talented individuals from 30+ different nationalities. We work seamlessly together with colleagues around the corner, across the organisation and between offices in Asia, Africa, Latin America and Europe.

About Impact Fund Denmark

Impact Fund Denmark (IFU – the Investment Fund for Developing Countries) is a Danish impact investor contributing to green, just and inclusive societies as well as supporting the Sustainable Development Goals. Impact Fund Denmark provides risk capital to companies operating in developing countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and parts of Europe. Investments are made on commercial terms in the form of equity, loans and guarantees. Impact Fund Denmark has co-invested in over 1,300 companies in more than 100 developing countries and emerging markets. Contracted investments total EUR 31 billion, of which Impact Fund Denmark has contributed EUR 3.4 billion. Capital under management will be growing from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 5.0 billion over the next few years. Read more at Impact Fund Denmark

title: Assistant Professor in Energy Harvesting and EMI Mitigation in High-Voltage Environments - 4391
description:
The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for an Assistant Professor position in Energy Harvesting and EMI Mitigation for Drones and Robots in High-Voltage Environments. The position is open from January 1, 2027, and the starting date will be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

Job Content

The Assistant Professor will conduct research within energy harvesting for drones, robotic systems, and IoT applications, with a particular focus on enhancing power density and enabling long-term autonomous operation. The research will further address electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) for electronic and robotic systems operating in extreme high-voltage environments, contributing to improved system reliability, safety, and performance in infrastructure inspection and maintenance applications.

The successful candidate is expected to develop and sustain a research agenda aligned with or complementing the section’s activities, establish an internationally recognized research profile, publish in high-impact journals and leading international conference proceedings, and actively contribute to securing external research funding from national and international sources. The role includes collaboration with academic colleagues and industrial partners and participation in national and international research activities.

The position includes planning, teaching, and developing Bachelor’s and Master’s-level courses in relevant areas of electronics and electrical engineering. The successful candidate will supervise Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD students, provide academic guidance, and contribute to a supportive and collaborative research and learning environment. The role also includes academic service at section and department levels and participation in relevant professional activities.

 

Required Qualifications

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in Electronics Engineering, Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field.

Applicants must document the following qualifications and experience:

  • A strong research track record in electromagnetic energy harvesting, power conversion, or power management systems.

  • Research experience in electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) for operation in extreme high-voltage environments up to 500 kV.

  • Experience in the design, development, and testing of drone systems.

  • Experience in university teaching, course development, and supervision of engineering students, together with pedagogical and subject-specific skills appropriate to the position.

  • A proven ability to attract external research funding as principal investigator or key contributor.

  • A strong publication record in leading international journals and conferences, including publications resulting from international collaborations.

  • Demonstrated experience in international research projects and collaborative activities with academic and industrial partners.

  • Experience serving as reviewer for leading international journals and conferences in relevant research fields.

International research experience gained in an environment other than the institution where the applicant completed their PhD will be considered an advantage.

 

Workplace description

The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics at the University of Southern Denmark conducts research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communications, using advanced reconfigurable computing and sensing technologies. The section develops next-generation electronics and computing solutions to address technological challenges in autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grids, and healthcare.

The section contributes to the electrical engineering programmes in Odense, including Bachelor’s and Master of Science degrees in Electronics Engineering. Over the next few years, the section is expected to expand to at least 30 staff members, including academic staff, PhD students, and engineers, supporting research, industrial collaboration, and education. This growth will strengthen the section’s contribution to electrical engineering and related fields.

SDU’s Odense campus comprises six faculties, providing opportunities for interdisciplinary research and a vibrant student life. Odense offers a culturally rich environment, a growing robotics community, attractive residential areas, and green spaces along the river through the city centre.

Further Information

For further information about the position, please contact Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, Head of the Section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics, at esme@sdu.dk. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Motivated application that clearly explains the applicant’s interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages).

  • Curriculum Vitae, including contact information, research experience, relevant projects, technical skills, and teaching and supervision experience.

  • Research plan outlining the proposed research agenda, its alignment with the position and the section’s activities, and plans for developing a research line and research team.

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation). 

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Publications most relevant to the position. 

  • Summary and documentation of teaching qualifications, pedagogical experience, course development, and student supervision. You may attach a Teaching Portfolio. 

  • Names and email addresses of up to three referees who can provide an informed reference at short notice. Reference letters and documentation of other relevant qualifications may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

title: PhD Position in Energy Harvesting for Bio-Inspired Flying Robots
description:
The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics in Odense at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a PhD position in energy harvesting for bio-inspired flying robots. The position focuses on developing energy-harvesting techniques that use the magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines to support autonomous inspection of power lines. The starting date is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.  

This is a three-year PhD position based at SDU’s campus in Odense, Denmark.

The section focuses on conducting research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communication, utilizing cutting-edge reconfigurable computing and sensors. The aim is to develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions that solve technology-related challenges in fields such as autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grid, and healthcare.

The section contributes to our educational programmes in electrical engineering in Odense, offering Bachelor’s and Master of Science degrees in Electronics Engineering. Its activities span research, industrial collaboration, and education in electrical engineering and related areas.

The SDU campus in Odense comprises six faculties, bringing together academics and students in an environment that supports interdisciplinary research and a rich student life. Odense offers a vibrant robotics community, cultural activities, attractive residential areas, and green spaces along the river that runs through the city centre.

 

Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the FreeFly project, an ambitious research project focused on developing a bird-like flying robot for autonomous inspection of power lines. The PhD research will focus on energy harvesting to enable self-sustaining operation of this bio-inspired robotic platform.

Research Focus – Energy Harvesting for Bio-Inspired Flying Robots

You will investigate, analyse, and design novel energy-harvesting techniques that enable bio-inspired aerial robots to draw energy from the strong magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines. Your research will contribute to the development of self-sustaining flying robotic systems, with the aim of enabling extended autonomous inspection missions.

General Responsibilities

As a PhD student on this project, you will:

  • Conduct research on energy harvesting from the magnetic fields surrounding high-voltage power lines, contributing to the development of a self-sustaining, bird-like autonomous flying robot for inspection of power lines.

  • Participate in teaching activities, including course planning and instruction in relevant subject areas.

  • Collaborate closely with fellow PhD students, postdocs, and other members of the research group in a dynamic, interdisciplinary environment.

We are looking for a detail-oriented, self-driven candidate with a strong interest in energy harvesting and its application to bio-inspired flying robots. If you are motivated to contribute to innovative research in autonomous inspection of power lines, we encourage you to apply.

 

Required Qualifications

  • A completed BSc and MSc in electronics, electrical engineering, physics, mechatronics, or a closely related discipline. Applicants in the final semester of their master’s programme are also encouraged to apply, provided they complete their MSc before the starting date and meet the applicable PhD admission requirements.

  • Strong technical skills relevant to energy harvesting, particularly magnetic-field energy harvesting, electronics, and embedded hardware architectures.

  • Demonstrated ability in academic writing, including preparing scientific reports, documentation, and research publications.

For further information about the position, please contact the Head of Digital and High-frequency Electronics section, Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, e-mail: esme@sdu.dk.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Motivated application that clearly explains the applicant’s interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages). 

  • Detailed Curriculum Vitae, including personal contact information, skills, along with any other relevant information, e.g. teaching experience, computational skills, relevant projects, etc.

  • Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation). Applicants in the final semester of their master’s programme are requested to submit transcripts from all completed semesters. 

  • Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

  • An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

  • Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

  • List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

  • Up to three names and emails of researchers who can provide an informed reference letter at short notice. (Reference letters and other relevant qualifications may also be included.)

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.313 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step.

The preferred start date is from January 1, 2027. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

title: Mechanic, HGV Mechanic or Welder wanted for varied role in Glostrup
description:

title: Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead; DK - Frederikshavn
description:
Do you have a strong electrical background and are you motivated by technical leadership and the opportunity to help shape the construction of Denmark’s new Arctic ships? As Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead at Semco Maritime, you will take ownership of the electrical installation scope in a nationally significant naval project.Your position In this role, you will be part of a multidisciplinary team working closely with design, procurement, fabrication, and quality control. You will help turn technical requirements and design into practical, high-quality installation solutions and ensure efficient production throughout all phases of shipbuilding, in compliance with naval and classification standards. The final title will depend on your experience and qualifications.Your work will have a direct impact on the successful delivery of the Arctic ships and on the continued development of the Danish naval shipbuilding industry.The position will be based in Frederikshavn, where the Arctic ships will be assembled, and is a full-time, permanent position.Your tasks & responsibilities As Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead you will plan, coordinate, and lead the electrical installation scope throughout ship production, ensuring alignment between engineering, procurement, suppliers, and production teams.Your tasks will include, but are not limited to:
  • Defining and planning electrical installation methods from design through production, including installation sequencing, equipment installation, and coordination with relevant stakeholders
  • Participating in the production engineering process to support quality, safety, and efficiency
  • Supporting the development of electrical discipline project plans and resource estimates
  • Lead parts of the installations scope when in construction
  • Acting as the technical point of contact internally and with suppliers for electrical and instrumentation matters
  • Providing technical input to procurement and defining requirements for electrical installation equipment and tools
  • Ensuring compliance with naval, military, and classification standards as well as health, safety, and environmental requirements
Your profile & qualificationsWe are looking for a proactive and responsible engineer who can act as lead by combining strong technical understanding with hands-on problem-solving skills.You work in a structured and quality-focused way, communicate clearly across disciplines, and bring high personal integrity and strong safety awareness.Even if you do not meet all the desired experience requirements, we encourage you to apply if you believe you are a talented individual with the right mindset, strong motivation, and a willingness to learn and grow in the roleTo succeed in this role, we expect that you have:
  • A BSc or MSc in marine or electrical engineering
  • Solid experience in shipbuilding, heavy industry or offshore projects (oil and gas / wind)
  • Min. 5 years relevant experience
  • Familiarity with international classification rules, such as DNV or ABS
  • Fluency in English, written and spoken
  • Danish language skills
  • Knowledge of naval or defence standards would be an advantage
Welcome to Semco MaritimeAt Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the planet. By joining us, you will become part of a community of over 2,300 dedicated thinkers and doers who drive meaningful change and leave their mark on the world. Change is essential, and we always keep our eyes on the journey - how to get there.We provide the answers needed to make change real, believing that ambitious goals can only be achieved through hard work and innovative, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a better future.So yes, working for us will spark change – and may well change you too.Care to join the movement?Change. With us.Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

title: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
description:
About the positionThe Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.Key responsibilitiesStrategic leadership and governance

  • Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

  • Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

  • Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

  • Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state.

  • Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices.

  • Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.

Operational responsibility

  • Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication.

  • Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.

About youTo succeed in this role, we expect that you:

  • Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage.

  • Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

  • Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions.

  • Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

  • Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.

In addition, you:

  • Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations.

  • Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries.

  • Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.

About the Danish Resilience AgencyThe Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.About the NBCCThe NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.Salary and terms of employmentSalary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. Non-EU/EEA Citizens must hold a valid residence and work permit before you can begin working in Denmark. Citizens of Sweden, Norway, Finland, or Iceland do not require a residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark. title: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

  1. A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

  2. Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

  3. Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

  4. Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

  5. A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: Assistant Professor in Global Health at The Research Unit of General Practice, University of Southern Denmark
description:
The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health. The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Beskrivelse til interne kandidater

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Job DescriptionThe position involves research in global health with a particular focus on strengthening primary healthcare systems for vulnerable and underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries. The successful candidate will contribute to the international research project STRENGTHENing Gender-Responsive Health Systems for Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases in Climate-Affected Fishing Communities in Western Kenya (STRENGTHEN) and other upcoming global health projects. The STRENGTHEN project aims to improve the prevention and management of NCDs in climate-affected fishing communities in Western Kenya by making the health systems even more gender-responsive. The project will generate evidence on how community health promoters (CHPs) provide NCD care in FEDCs affected by climate change. It will address five key health systems building blocks: health information systems, health workforce, health service, medical technology, and policy and governance. The work will involve conducting implementation and health services research, and collaborating with researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and community stakeholders across different country settings. The position involves travel to Kenya for short periods.

We offer a challenging position in a stimulating research environment with excellent opportunities for collaboration within SDU and with international research partners.

Expectations of qualificationsThe successful applicant should have:

  • A PhD degree (or equivalent) in Global Health, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Services Research, Implementation Science, or a related discipline

  • A strong background in health systems research, primary healthcare, chronic disease prevention and management, or health equity research in low- and middle-income countries

  • A strong academic record

  • Good collaboration and communication skills

  • Interest in co-supervising BSc, MSc and PhD students

Following qualifications are preferred:

  • Experience with mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis

  • Experience with implementation science, intervention development, and evaluation of community-based health programmes

  • Experience with global health research conducted in low- and middle-income countries and/or humanitarian settings

  • Experience with stakeholder engagement and collaboration with healthcare providers, communities, and policymakers

  • Experience with writing research applications

  • Experience in teaching and education

Further informationFor further information please contact Prof. Jens Søndergaard, jsondergaard@health.sdu.dk, or Associate Prof. Trine Thilsing, tthilsing@health.sdu.dk 

Application deadline and interviewsThe application deadline is November15th 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)  

Terms of employment Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from 1. April 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme, if this has not already been completed.   

Appointment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. 

Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations .

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.  

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Application Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.  

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.  

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.  

Your application must include the following as PDF files: 

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total). 

  • a motivation letter.  

  • a detailed CV.  

  • degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma). 

  • a complete and numbered list of publications.  

  • 3 to 5 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.  

    • It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file. 

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy.  

  • a research plan an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position. 

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered. 

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Assessment and selection process Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

About UsThe Research Unit of General Practice is a collaboration between the Research Unit of General Practice in Odense-Esbjerg, which is organizationally affiliated with the Foundation for General Practice Research (FEA), and the Research Unit of General Practice at the Department of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU).

The primary objective of the Research Unit is to contribute to the improvement and development of health and healthcare for patients, with a particular focus on services provided in and around general practice. 

A cornerstone of our educational activities is the training of Master's and PhD students. In addition, we contribute to teaching across a range of health sciences bachelor's and master's degree programmes at the Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, as well as within the Research Training Programme of the specialist training programme in general practice.

Further information about The Faculty of Health Sciences.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years.
description:
A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

  • Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

  • Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

  • Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

  • Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

  • Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

  • Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

  • A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

  • First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

  • Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

  • Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

  • A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

  • Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

  • The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

  • Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

  • Experience in psychiatric epidemiology.

  • Experience in the development or validation of prediction models.

  • Practical experience with target trial emulation.

  • Experience in international research collaborations.

  • Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

title: Experienced High Voltage Specialist wanted for Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst
description:
Do you have at least three years of high voltage experience? At Bravida, you will install circuit breakers, disconnectors and switchboards and help build substations. Here, you will put your experience to use on critical electrical infrastructure projects that help secure Denmark’s power supply and support the green transition.

On behalf of Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst, Career | a JKS Company is recruiting experienced High Voltage Specialists for projects across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst has secured the framework agreement with Energinet, becoming a regular supplier of high voltage installation work across Zealand and Lolland-Falster. With this agreement and a strong order book, Bravida is expanding the department. You will join the team responsible for building, expanding, refurbishing and maintaining the infrastructure that the power grid of the future relies on.

Installation and construction of high voltage installationsYou will work at substations and other high voltage installations, putting your experience into practice. You will take responsibility for your own tasks and work alongside your team to deliver safe, high-quality work.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Installing and replacing circuit breakers, disconnectors and other substation components

  • Carrying out cable work and working on earthing systems

  • Working on switchboards, electrical installations and dismantling tasks

  • Contributing to the construction, refurbishment and maintenance of high voltage installations

  • Carrying out quality assurance and maintaining documentation

Over time, you will also share your knowledge by helping apprentices and new colleagues get to grips with their tasks.

You bring solid high voltage experience and take responsibilityYou are a qualified electrician or have an equivalent electrical qualification, with at least three years of hands-on experience in high voltage work. You are familiar with the tasks described and comfortable working independently. You take initiative, recognise what needs doing and understand that safety is integral to every task.

We are looking for someone who:

  • Works independently and takes a structured approach

  • Takes responsibility for the safety and quality of their work

  • Is proactive, well-presented and works well with others

  • Is physically fit and comfortable with hands-on work outdoors and at height

  • Holds a category B driving licence and can provide a criminal record certificate

You must be able to communicate clearly in English and have a valid work permit for Denmark.

A company vehicle to take home and no on-call dutiesAt Bravida, you will join a team of skilled, dedicated technicians who take pride in their work.

You will work daytime hours with no on-call duties, normally five days a week. Start times depend on the project, and the working week can be discussed. The role is paid hourly, with pay based on qualifications, plus pension contributions and a flexible benefits allowance under the Danish “fritvalgsordning” scheme.

You will have a company vehicle equipped with the tools and equipment you need, which you can take home. Your exact location is therefore less important, provided you are willing to work at different sites across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

We look forward to hearing from youIf this sounds like the right role for you, please send us your CV. We review applications and invite suitable candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, and will close the vacancy once the right candidates have been found.

title: Associate Professor in Public Health: Children and Young People
description:
At the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), a position as Associate Professor in Public Health is hereby advertised with a focus on interdisciplinary, qualitative studies of children’s and young people’s health and well-being, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.About your future research environment  

The National Institute of Public Health (NIPH) is part of the University of Southern Denmark and is located in Copenhagen. As a national public health institute, we conduct research to improve public health in Denmark and Greenland. At the same time, we contribute internationally to the development of knowledge, theories and methods in the field of public health.

We offer an inspiring research environment in the heart of Copenhagen with skilled and dedicated colleagues from diverse research and educational backgrounds. Here, you will have the opportunity for academic exchange and further development of your own research areas, as well as participation in national and international networks. The position is anchored in the research group Health Promotion and Interventions, which conducts research on interventions addressing public health issues and works with methodological and theoretical challenges related to the design and evaluation of intervention and implementation studies. Our research concerns children, young people and families, as well as vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, and takes place in a range of settings, including daycare institutions, primary and lower secondary schools, upper secondary education, the healthcare system, municipal services, supermarkets and local communities.  You will actively participate in the daily activities of the research group and work closely with other researchers at NIPH.  

The duties include research, teaching and dissemination within the institute’s areas of expertise, including:  - Children’s and young people’s health, well-being and everyday life- The significance of digital media for children’s and young people’s lives and health- Health promotion and implementation research in daycare institutions, schools and upper secondary education- Interdisciplinary, practice-oriented research and development projects, including process evaluation- Advanced qualitative methods, including ethnography, interviews, focus groups and child-centred approaches- Teaching and supervision at bachelor’s and master’s level, including qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and implementation- Preparation of applications for external funding as well as project management and coordination- Contributions to the further development of the research environment, including method development and research group activities The following qualifications are highly valued:  You have established yourself as a qualified researcher within qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and intervention and implementation research, and you possess strong research and teaching qualifications at a high level. You have a relevant publication profile and extensive experience in disseminating research to researchers, practitioners, and other target groups. You have broad collaborative networks and experience in research collaboration with practitioners. As a person, you are dedicated and possess strong communication skills. You are able to build trusting relationships with students, colleagues, and external partners alike. As a teacher, you communicate up-to-date, relevant knowledge in an engaging, clear and understandable way, and as a supervisor you are skilled, inspiring, and supportive.  Qualifications  - A PhD degree in Public Health, Education, Sociology, Anthropology or a related field- Experience with intervention and implementation research- Documented experience in research on children’s and young people’s health- A strong profile within qualitative research- Experience in collaborating with practitioners, exchanging knowledge and disseminating research- Experience in national and international research collaboration- Documented teaching experience at university level and experience supervising students (e.g. bachelor’s or master's students)- Proficiency in Danish and English at a high level, both orally and in writing- Documented experience with scientific publications within relevant research areas 

Further information regarding the position can be obtained from:  Research Leader Susan Andersen,  mailto:suan@sdu.dk

Terms and conditions of employment  Appointment as an Associate Professor is for a fixed term of three years, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.Appointment to the position will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for associate professor as described herein. Please check links for more information on salary (only available in Danish) and taxation.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

The assessment and evaluation processShortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material. Interviews and tests may form part of the overall assessment carried out by the appointment committee.  Based on information from the entire recruitment process, the Head of Institute will decide which applicant is offered the position. 

The application

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. 

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

  • Motivated application

  • Curriculum vitae

  • Master’s degree and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original + verified English translation)

  • Teaching portfolio

  • Research plan, including an account of your own research and preferably a vision for future research 

  • A complete list of publications

  • Up to six of the most relevant publications. Please attach one PDF file per publication. In cases of co-authorship, a co-author declaration must be submitted as part of the PDF file.

  • Reference letters/references may also be included

  • A statement of other qualifications relevant to the position.

We request files in pdf-format no more than 5 MB per file. All pdf-files must be unlocked and allow merging and may not be password protected. Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application shall be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae shall be uploaded as ‘CV’. All other documents shall be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’.

If the application does not meet the requirements mentioned above, the faculty may reject your application without further notice. Applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated.

If you experience technical problems, please contact mailto:hcm-support@sdu.dkApplication deadline 18 November 2026 at 23.59 (CET) 

We recommend that as an international applicant, you take the time to visit Work in Denmark where you will find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark, as well as the International Staff Office at SDU.  The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding society and therefore encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.  

About SDU  The University of Southern Denmark was founded to create value for and together with society. Whether our contribution comes in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education, or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by nurturing talent and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops, and recruits talented individuals. At the same time, we must ensure consistently high quality in all our activities, which can only be achieved with the right people.  The university’s researchers, teachers, students, managers, and technical-administrative staff constitute the foundation of our success.

title: Production Worker - Nakskov (Day/night)

Would you like to help ensure a more sustainable future? Vestas is currently looking for unskilled workers with experience in production work.   • Safety: At Vestas, safety is the first priority, which means you must prioritize your own and your colleagues' safety, both physically and mentally.

  • Quality: Our next priority is top-notch quality, so we expect you to take pride in producing a product that meets standards.

  • Production Plan: At Vestas, we also have some plans that need to be met to deliver on time. So, we expect an employee who is diligent and strives to meet deadlines without compromising safety or quality.

Qualifications

  • You are in good physical shape and accustomed to standing and walking throughout the workday.

  • It is advantageous if you have experience with 5S and Lean.

  • It is advantageous if you have experience with production work, but if you are willing to learn, we would like to hear from you.

Competencies

  • You are quality-conscious and focus on safety.

  • You contribute to creating a good atmosphere at work.

  • You don't mind changing tasks.

  • You have an interest in learning new things and are curious.

We OfferA workplace with a focus on employees, their safety, and providing them with the tools to create quality in their work. We offer an attractive salary package with health insurance, dental insurance, and a canteen arrangement. Additional Information

  • Workplace: Nakskov

Our commitment to a fair hiring. At Vestas, we evaluate all candidates solely based on their professional experience, education, and relevant skills. To support a fair recruitment process, we kindly ask that you remove any photos, dates of birth or graduation, gender pronouns, marital status, or other personal information not relevant to the role before submitting your CV/resume. Your CV/resume should focus on your professional and educational background, along with the necessary contact details (email and phone number). We train our hiring teams in inclusive evaluation and regularly review process outcomes to ensure fairness.DEIB Statement At Vestas, we recognize the value of diversity, equity, and inclusion in driving innovation and success. As our CEO states, "Expertise and talent come in many forms, and a diverse workforce enhances our ability to think differently and solve the complex challenges of our industry". Your unique perspective is what will help us powering the solution for a sustainable, green energy future.BEWARE – RECRUITMENT FRAUDIt has come to our attention that there are a number of fraudulent emails from people pretending to work for Vestas. Read more via this link, https://www.vestas.com/en/careers/our-recruitment-process About VestasVestas is the energy industry’s global partner on sustainable energy solutions. Kannatlikku ja järjekindlat – mõistad, et kvaliteetne taastamistöö nõuab aega, pühendumist ja täpsust. Iseseisvat ja vastutustundlikku – oskad oma tööd planeerida, võtad vastutuse tulemuse eest ja pead kokkulepetest kinni. Õpihimulist ja arenemissooviga – tunned huvi uute töövõtete vastu ja soovid oma meisterlikkust pidevalt täiendada. Positiivset ja meeskonnahingega – oled sõbralik, koostööaldis ja aitad kaasa heale töökeskkonnale. Kõige olulisem on, et sul oleks tõeline huvi autode taastamise ja plekitöö vastu, head käelised oskused ning soov teha tööd, mille üle saad ise uhkust tunda.

Gravenori Pärnu esinduses tegeleme lisaks tehnika hooldusele ja remondile suuremate ümberehituste, pealisehituste ning kliendi vajadustele loodud erilahendustega. Ühel päeval võib töös olla tõstuki või rasketehnika remont, järgmisel hüdraulika- või elektrisüsteemi ümberehitus ning seejärel suurem projekt, kus masinale tuleb sobiv lahendus valmistada, paigaldada ja tööle seadistada. title: Senior AI Engineer (image & video generation)
description:
Working language: English (Estonian not required). Remote; Tallinn optional.

Work tasks: MyArchitectAI is AI rendering software for architects and interior designers. Users upload a design and get a photorealistic render in seconds that keeps their geometry and materials. Then they can swap materials, change lighting and objects, upscale, or turn the still into a video. We're a small founder-led team and we move fast. Our working language is English. We're looking for an engineer who rapidly turns promising image- and video-generation techniques into evaluated, shipped MyArchitectAI features. This is hands-on product building: not pure research, and not a pure inference/infrastructure job. - In your first 30 days you ship a meaningful improvement, scoped with a founder: a new AI capability, a quality or speed gain, an evaluation system, or automation of manual work. You back it with visual examples and numbers. - By 60 days you find an opportunity yourself (new models, user data, weak spots in our pipeline), propose it and ship it. - By 90 days you have three or more shipped contributions and own the loop: find → evaluate → build → validate → ship → learn. - You keep a clear view of new models, techniques and competitors without chasing novelty for its own sake.

We offer: - Working directly with the founders, with real impact on the product.- GPU access. - Remote work; Tallinn optional. - Employment contract or contractor agreement, as you prefer. - English is our working language; Estonian is not required. - Salary negotiable.

Other requirements: You have:- Hands-on work with generative image or video models (not only LLMs, RAG or agents). - At least one shipped product, deployed feature, meaningful open-source contribution, or convincing end-to-end project, and you can say exactly what you built. - Experience running experiments and making quality vs. speed vs. cost decisions. - The engineering skills to take a notebook or demo into a real product (Python, production-quality code). - Good written English (our working language). Estonian is not required. Nice to have: Diffusers, ComfyUI, ControlNet-style conditioning, inpainting and editing, LoRA and fine-tuning, video models, upscaling; your own evaluation datasets or benchmarks; GPU deployment and optimisation; 3D, AEC, CAD, rendering or interiors; public code, demos, models or write-ups.
